findings: The adult ash-gray body and contrasting glossy black head, throat, wings, and tail match the diagnostic Hooded Crow pattern shown in the references and described by eBird and Wikipedia.
The primary specimen has one head, one coherent bill, two folded wings—the far wing visible as a subordinate layered portion—two plausibly attached legs with grasping feet, and one tail.

The primary bill is stout and proportionate; both mandibles trace coherently from the shared base to the tip. The detached head study is consistent with the primary head and the clearest side-profile references.
The tail is now medium-length and terminates in a substantially square edge rather than the previously long, rounded profile.
Both depicted irises read as dark brown, with normal highlights, rather than conspicuous amber.
The detached extended-wing study is anatomically coherent, clearly supplementary, and does not appear attached to the primary specimen.

Every visible profile line was checked: common name, scientific name, family, all three measurements, habitat, behavior, six field marks, and four palette labels are correctly spelled and agree with the proposed wording and values.
The ruler increases from 48 cm at the bottom to 52 cm at the top, agrees with the printed body-length range, uses the correct units, and is explicitly labeled “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE.”
The plate contains no place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail.
